steps.question: Do AD-lesional samples show a shifted immune cell composition (e.g. increased T cell, dendritic cell, or myeloid infiltrate) relative to control skin, consistent with AD's known inflammatory infiltrate?
acceptance_criteria: Runs bulk immune deconvolution (e.g. via the immunedeconv wrapper, using a method such as quanTIseq, EPIC, MCPcounter, or xCell already available in the sandbox) on the normalized 12000x12 expression matrix
Reports estimated immune/stromal cell fractions per sample, grouped by condition (AD-lesional vs control)

Explicitly notes this is skin tissue, not the tumor microenvironment these deconvolution signatures were often built for, and flags any cell types poorly represented by the chosen signature matrix for skin

plan.title: AD lesional vs control skin DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a single gene-level count table (12000 genes x 12 samples: 6 AD-lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) produced from Salmon, but per-sample quant.sf files were not delivered and it is unknown whether the counts already incorporate Salmon's average-transcript-length offset (the standard tximport countsFromAbundance='lengthScaledTPM' or 'no' path) or are raw estimated counts. Soneson, Love & Robinson (2015, F1000Research) established that gene-level counts derived from transcript quantifiers require a length-based offset to avoid inflated false-discovery rates when isoform usage differs between conditions — but that offset can only be reconstructed from per-transcript effective lengths, which are not available here. Track 1 therefore first inspects the count table itself (row sums, fractional vs integer values, distribution) to determine empirically whether it looks like raw Salmon counts (fractional, NB-suitable) versus something already normalized, and flags this rather than assuming. Track 1 then proceeds with a standard DESeq2 workflow treating the values as counts (the only tractable path given no quant.sf files), explicitly documenting the caveat that isoform-driven length bias cannot be corrected or ruled out. This is followed by apeglm shrinkage for interpretable fold changes, a full DE table, diagnostic PCA/dispersion plots, and a volcano plot. Track 2 takes the DE gene list into pathway/hallmark enrichment (WikiPathways human + MSigDB hallmark, both available locally) to characterize the AD-lesional biology (expected Th2/IL-13, keratinocyte differentiation, barrier genes per Tsoi et al. 2019, PMID 30641038), and separately performs immune cell deconvolution given AD's known immune infiltrate, using bulk deconvolution tools present in the sandbox. All steps are scoped to the 12000-gene x 12-sample matrix actually delivered; no external validation cohort is pulled in since GEO search for a matching AD RNA-seq design returned no directly comparable dataset in this session.
